title: What to eat
intro: Uruguayan food centers on the parrilla (wood-fired grill) — beef, but also the chivito (a stacked steak sandwich with ham, cheese, egg, and olives) as the national fast-food answer to it. Wine means Tannat, the country's signature red grape.

items.name: El Palenque
items.how: Inside Mercado del Puerto, a 5–10 min walk from Plaza Independencia
items.crowd_tip: Arrive right at opening for lunch — by 13:00 on a weekend it's standing-room only at the grill counters.
items.why: Ranked among Bloomberg's top parrillas in the world; the everyday standard-bearer for Uruguayan grilled beef.

items.name: El Palenque (Punta del Este branch)
items.address: Parada 7, Av. Roosevelt, Punta del Este
items.how: On the main beach avenue, best reached by taxi from central Punta del Este
items.why: The same house on the coast — a fallback if Montevideo's queue was too long the first time.

items.name: Bodega Bouza
items.address: Cno. de la Redención 7658 bis, Montevideo
items.hours: ⚠ Reported daily 11:00–18:00; not independently confirmed which day(s) are closed — confirm before visiting on a holiday
items.how: Taxi or rideshare from downtown Montevideo — no direct bus
items.price: ⚠ ≈UYU 2,800/person for the guided tasting tour (unconfirmed against the winery's own current pricing)
items.why: A boutique Tannat producer with vintage cars on display and a vineyard-to-glass lunch — the closest thing to a proper wine-country morning without leaving greater Montevideo.

items.name: Lo de Silverio
items.area: Villa Dolores, away from the port tourist core
items.address: Alejo Rossell y Rius 1655 esq. 4 de Julio, Montevideo
items.how: Taxi or rideshare from downtown — a residential neighborhood, not a walk from Ciudad Vieja
items.price: ⚠ ask when booking — not listed online
items.why: A neighborhood parrilla off the tourist circuit, in residential Villa Dolores — book ahead for dinner, capacity is limited.
